locations.note: Returns as Laguna Seca Raceway, and hosts the 90-lap Laguna Seca 200 Miles in the endurance series.
Nordschleife, GP, GP/D, Type V and the combined 24h course, which brings night and changing weather to a full 24 Hours of Nürburgring endurance race.
2005 and 2009 layouts, each with and without the Mulsanne chicanes; the 2009 track adds night and weather for a full 24 Hours of Le Mans.
Hosts two endurance races, a 4-hour race for roadsters and the Tsukuba 9 Hours.
Full circuit and East Course; a version of the full circuit with changing weather hosts the Suzuka 1000 km endurance race.
New to the series in GT5, as both the oval and the road course; the road course was the pre-release demo track and the oval runs a 200-lap Indy 500.
New to the series in GT5, with a version that has changing weather and a separate layout without the chicanes.
Both the superspeedway oval and the road course, in the game that brought licensed NASCAR racing to the series.
Top Gear's test track appears only in GT5, with a special event that races VW Samba buses, a Lotus Elise and VW Kübelwagens around it.
Only the modern track remains, in its F and GT layouts; the 1980s and 1990s versions from GT4 are gone.
A 3.5 km Rome street circuit, new in this layout for GT5 and raced in both directions, that winds past the Colosseum.
New to GT5: the Circuito de Madrid street course, raced in both directions, with a shorter Mini layout.
A short street circuit from GT5 Prologue, raced in both directions, past Piccadilly Circus, along Regent Street and Charing Cross Road to Trafalgar Square.
Tokyo R246 follows real roads in Akasaka, including Route 246 itself, in both directions; it was the track of the Gamescom 2009 demo.
Raced as Côte d'Azur, a version of the Monaco Grand Prix street circuit around the harbour.
A tarmac Short Track with changing weather below the Eiger's north face, plus K, G and W Trails on snow and dirt, all raced in both directions.
Snow and dirt course with Main, East, West and Mini layouts, all with changing weather.
Toscana, a dirt course through the Tuscan countryside with a changing time of day, raced in both directions.
Added after release in the Track Pack DLC, with changing weather.
Twin Ring Motegi returned to the series as DLC in June 2012, after that year's GT Academy.
